title: Run Claude and Codex together through cdx

needs: Make the fork a hub for both Claude Code and Codex, with one cdx profile per account and simultaneous sessions across registered projects.
Choose a provider/account explicitly for interactive work, brief, project handoff and tracked background jobs; retain existing Claude-only configurations.
Observe activity, usage, quotas and interrupted work for both providers in existing CLI, terminal board and optional widgets.
Continue a chosen task across providers using verified context transfer, with account policy and workspace ownership preserved.
context: Repository inspection on 2026-10-22: interactive launches already call cdx, but crow-runs detects only Claude processes and parses Claude messages; crow-usage scans Claude profile paths, imports private cdx_manager.run_usage helpers and defaults to a direct Claude title command; crow-sessions, crow-memory and retros also assume Claude layouts.

The installed cdx-manager 0.21.4 exposes both providers, cdx --json, schema --json, select --provider --require-ready --json, status --cached --json, run, run-status, run-report, runs, history, stats, can-resume and handoff. This is an inspected compatibility baseline, not an assertion about earlier releases. Capture sanitized fixtures and gate required capabilities before advertising support.

cdx run publishes schema_version, ok, provider, session, run_id, exit_code, stdout_path, transcript_path and nullable token usage. Consume its public JSON boundary; no import of cdx Python internals or assumption that the executable is a Python script.

Installed cdx handoff supports Claude and Codex native transcripts. SOURCE TARGET --source-conversation ID --json prepares an entry without launching; --source-native-transcript PATH disambiguates duplicate native IDs. Native resume remains provider-specific. Cross-provider handoff starts a target conversation and links it to the source.

OpenAI official non-interactive and CLI documentation was checked on 2026-10-22 for exec JSON events and resume. Crow delegates execution to cdx; native event parsing is a bounded read-only fallback for activity details missing from cdx, versioned with synthetic fixtures. No Codex API key is required for corpus creation.

Existing account-switching task_002 is In progress. Reuse its policy helper, interrupted registry and memory behavior; add provider-aware migrations without closing, resetting or duplicating that work. The earlier UI corpus owns layout improvements; this request adds provider identity and mixed data to those surfaces.

Scope decision: joint use means concurrent Claude/Codex tasks, explicit provider selection and guarded cross-provider task handoff. Autonomous agent-to-agent conversation, consensus loops and automatic cross-provider retries are excluded.

Architecture decision: add a small shared Python boundary under bin/ for cdx invocation, provider capabilities and normalized records; keep Bash launcher, Go TUI and QML consumers. cdx owns auth homes and launches; crow owns its allowed-account policy, task lineage and presentation.

Private config, raw transcripts, handoff entries, memory and run state stay under ignored local/ or cdx-managed private storage. Public fixtures use invented profiles and temporary directories. Never commit credentials, actual account lists or private project context.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A versioned cdx boundary discovers provider and capabilities, validates JSON/error envelopes, rejects unsupported contracts with actionable diagnostics and works with the installed Node launcher without importing private cdx modules.

AC2: Account configuration resolves provider from cdx and supports optional checked provider declarations, existing defaults, policy use/ask-first/never and per-job explicit account/provider selection; mismatches, disabled, unknown and forbidden targets fail before launch.

AC3: Interactive hub/project sessions, one-shot brief, dispatch, report, wait, AFK jobs, title generation and retros work through cdx for either provider; existing Claude commands keep their behavior and provider-specific model or permission flags cannot silently cross providers.

AC4: One Claude and one Codex job run concurrently with distinct provider/account/native-conversation identities, correct lifecycle/report/cancellation handling and a single global background-slot limit; conflicting writes in one workspace are refused or use explicit separate worktrees.
AC5: CLI snapshots, watch and both optional widgets distinguish providers, preserve existing fields and represent missing activity/context/quota data as unknown rather than idle, healthy or zero.

AC6: Usage aggregation separates provider, account, model, project and day, deduplicates live/history/run observations, normalizes cumulative versus delta tokens, avoids double-counting cached/reasoning subsets and keeps unknown prices/quotas null with provenance.

AC7: Interrupted-session records carry provider and exact source identity. Same-provider resume and Claude-to-Codex/Codex-to-Claude handoff verify workspace and policy, require confirmation and reject ambiguous/stale sources; failed launch never marks a source as resumed.

AC8: Both providers receive applicable repository instructions, allowed shared memory and task state through an explicit context mechanism; temporary shared-account access is removed on exit/failure and concurrent sessions cannot unlink each other or write credentials into shared context.

AC9: Common hub guard requirements are mapped to each provider capability. Unsupported enforcement fails closed for guarded actions with a diagnostic; no silent promise that Claude hooks protect a Codex session and no reduction in approval or permission settings.

AC10: Offline Python and Go regressions and mixed-provider rendering fixtures pass; onboarding, migration, capability matrix and manual opt-in smoke steps cover Claude-only, Codex-only and mixed setups without requiring live credentials in automated checks.

product.title: One crow hub for Claude and Codex
product.overview: Run and observe Claude Code and Codex accounts together through cdx, choose the right provider for each task, and transfer interrupted work with its exact source context.
goals: Keep one workflow for mixed-provider interactive work and background jobs.
Show trustworthy activity and usage without treating missing provider data as zero.
Preserve account consent, private memory and repository guard behavior during launches and transfers.
Deliver incrementally over the current account-switching and UI work.
non_goals: Implementing a direct OpenAI or Anthropic API client or installing/logging into user accounts.
Merging provider-native conversation stores or converting Claude transcripts into Codex sessions.
Autonomous multi-agent debate, automatic provider fallback, automatic credit resets or a new dashboard layout.
Running two writers in the same working tree without isolation.

backlog_items.title: 2.1 Public cdx contract and provider-aware account policy
problem: Crow assumes a Python cdx installation and accounts without provider identity.
scope_in: Priority rationale: every subsequent slice depends on reliable provider resolution and one policy boundary.

Introduce a shared subprocess boundary with argv arrays, timeouts, exit/ok/schema checks, bounded errors and cached capability discovery. Keep providers as claude/codex internal enums; tolerate unrelated providers in inventory but refuse them as targets.

Read public cdx inventory/schema/config/status contracts using sanitized 0.21.4 fixtures. Preserve CROW_ACCOUNT and old default/name/policy/memory configuration; explicit account overrides default, optional --provider constrains the resolved account. When only provider is supplied, select only within allowed enabled profiles; never let cdx select an unrestricted account.

Extend docs/accounts.example.yaml with invented Claude/Codex profiles, provider mismatch validation and documented unknown-profile policy. Inventory reads must not log into, refresh auth or alter profiles.
scope_out: Changing cdx or provider authentication internals.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Claude-only legacy fixtures resolve the same default; mixed fixtures resolve both providers and an explicit matching account wins over defaults.
AC2: Missing CLI, timeout, non-JSON, ok=false, unsupported schema, disabled/unknown profiles and provider mismatch produce actionable errors before any launch subprocess.
AC3: A never account is rejected in every path; ask-first consent records the exact target and action and cannot be reused for another account.
AC4: A Node entrypoint fixture works without importing cdx_manager or assuming a Python shebang.

backlog_items.title: 2.2 Shared context and enforceable guard capabilities
problem: Claude memory paths and hooks do not establish equivalent instructions or permissions for Codex.
scope_in: Priority rationale: instructions and guard guarantees must exist before exposing Codex launch paths; depends on 2.1.

Inventory provider-independent instructions and memory references; preserve AGENTS.md -> LOGICS.md and existing Claude instructions. Do not overwrite AGENTS.md or generated Logics runtime artifacts with the full CLAUDE.md.

Reuse crow-memory private local/ source; choose supported cdx context/memory or bounded launch prompt references for Codex rather than writing a fake Claude memory directory. Include owner preferences and project instructions when available; explicit error for missing required references.

Map common crow-hub-guard requirements to tested provider enforcement capabilities. Codex support is enabled only for operations whose guard requirements can be enforced; expose unsupported guarded actions as unavailable until a verified mechanism exists.
Use per-launch context handles and locked/reference-counted temporary access for shared accounts, with cleanup on normal exit, signal and failed spawn; leave unrelated files untouched.
scope_out: Changing cdx or provider authentication internals.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Synthetic Claude and Codex launches receive the same required repo/task references while retaining their native instruction semantics.
AC2: Never profiles receive no memory links or context; concurrent shared sessions retain access until the last closes and cleanup is idempotent.
AC3: A missing enforcement capability blocks the affected operation before provider launch; fixtures prove no permission downgrade or full-access substitution.
AC4: No private memory body, auth material or actual profile path appears in public diagnostics or committed fixtures.

backlog_items.title: 2.3 Provider-aware launch dispatch and helper jobs
problem: Launcher output and helper jobs still assume a Claude result envelope or invoke Claude directly.
scope_in: Priority rationale: deliver usable Codex execution after 2.1 and 2.2, before observability surfaces.
Add consistent --account and --provider choices to hub, term, project handoff, dispatch and one-shot entry points; keep existing argument forms and CROW_ACCOUNT.

Use cdx run public envelopes and run-report for final text, artifact references and status; retain explicit provider-specific fallback parsing only where public data lacks a final message. Handle ok=false, failed spawn, nonzero exit, timeout and cancellation separately from successful completion.

Route briefs, digest/retro, AFK and generated titles through the same account policy and provider boundary. Remove implicit direct Claude execution; keep explicit CROW_TITLE_CMD override as a documented operator-owned legacy escape hatch, with no automatic invocation when no eligible account exists.

Maintain one atomic global CROW_MAX_RUNS budget across both providers including detached runs; add workspace writer ownership and require another worktree or explicit read-only capability for a conflicting job. Persist provider/account/native identity with run lineage.
Keep model identifiers and reasoning/permission capabilities provider-specific. Do not enable cdx --failover by default because its target ranking can exceed crow allowed-account consent.
scope_out: Changing cdx or provider authentication internals.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Mocked interactive, brief, dispatch, AFK, title and retro paths target each provider with valid argv and return its final report; old Claude invocations still pass.
AC2: Two isolated mixed-provider jobs occupy two shared slots and a third is refused at capacity, including a simultaneous-dispatch race.
AC3: Same-workspace writers are rejected before spawn; separate worktrees preserve each job cwd and branch.
AC4: Provider-incompatible model/permission choices, denied policy and missing consent fail without a ledger success entry; failed/cancelled jobs release slots.
AC5: Detached run returns run_id immediately and wait/report resolve the correct run without Claude-only stdout assumptions.

backlog_items.title: 2.4 Mixed-provider activity and session registry
problem: Live discovery scans only Claude processes and session identity is not qualified by provider.
scope_in: Priority rationale: establish trustworthy common data before usage and UI; depends on 2.1 and 2.3.

Define additive normalized session records with provider, account, native id, cwd, source, timestamps, nullable metrics and capability/availability information. Use (provider, account, native id) identity and separate run_id lineage.

Prefer cdx history/run-status/report identity and artifact metadata. Keep bounded read-only Claude/Codex native adapters for prompts/tool activity and interactive session discovery unavailable in public payloads; resolve profile paths from supported metadata, not a fixed /home glob.

Normalize working/waiting/finished/failed/interrupted/unknown states conservatively; a quiet file does not prove waiting for a human. Version parsers/cache by provider and tolerate partial final JSONL records and unknown event variants.
Deduplicate interactive process, transcript and dispatched-run observations; exclude automatic retro/title work from user interrupted sessions without hiding genuine user jobs.
scope_out: Changing cdx or provider authentication internals.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Synthetic simultaneous sessions from both providers appear once each; identical native ids under different providers/accounts do not collide.
AC2: Claude message/tool events and Codex session_meta/response_item/event_msg fixtures yield comparable prompts, actions, identity and timestamps with unknown fields retained as null.
AC3: Unreadable/deleted files, partial trailing JSONL, unknown events and inaccessible processes do not crash a snapshot or turn an unknown session into a completed job.
AC4: Unchanged transcript fixtures reuse incremental caches; only newly appended content is parsed where supported.

backlog_items.title: 2.5 Provider-aware usage quota and cost accounting
problem: Claude token categories, private pricing imports and fixed quota assumptions cannot be applied to Codex.
scope_in: Priority rationale: depends on 2.1 and 2.4; trustworthy measures precede presentation.

Consume public cdx stats/run usage and cached status with provenance and freshness; use versioned native fallback only for missing per-day/session detail. Remove private cdx_manager price-table imports.

Normalize Codex cumulative token updates versus per-turn deltas without summing cumulative snapshots; cached input and reasoning output are subsets, while Claude cache creation/read semantics stay distinct.

Version crow usage schema and cache; preserve old consumer fields additively, retain legacy frozen history without relabeling it as Codex, and invalidate/rebuild derived caches without modifying source transcripts.

Carry provider/account/model/project/day keys through rollups, quota windows, prices and savings. Use public price metadata when available or an explicit versioned crow-owned table; unknown model cost remains null with unpriced counts. Never infer Codex prices or quotas from Claude.
Separate list-price estimates from subscription charges; preserve time window/units/source, avoid cross-provider quota percentages or cache-saving calculations when incomparable.
scope_out: Changing cdx or provider authentication internals.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Hand-calculated mixed fixtures match token/day/project totals across repeated collection and session/run overlap; cumulative Codex snapshots count only once.
AC2: Unknown cost/limits remain null throughout rollups rather than zero; partially priced totals identify incomplete coverage.
AC3: Provider-specific cache and reasoning fixtures prove subsets are not billed twice; frozen Claude history and existing usage regressions still pass.
AC4: Quota freshness/source and provider window labels remain visible in emitted JSON with no live auth refresh during normal polling.

backlog_items.title: 2.6 Exact resume and cross-provider task handoff
problem: The relaunch path assumes Claude native files and does not distinguish native resume from task transfer.
scope_in: Priority rationale: depends on 2.1, 2.2, 2.3 and 2.4; extends existing task_002 recovery without replacing it.

Migrate interrupted registry additively with provider, account, native conversation id, verified workspace and recovery mode. Legacy records resolve provider through inventory; unresolved identity remains unlaunchable.
Keep native resume capability separate from handoff capability: can-resume describes the target native resume strategy and must not incorrectly disqualify a valid cross-provider handoff.

For account/provider transfer prepare cdx handoff SOURCE TARGET --source-conversation ID --json in the verified workspace, inspect the preparation envelope, then launch the confirmed target. Duplicate ids require explicit native transcript selection. Never choose latest transcript by mtime.

Record confirmed source and target, resulting run/conversation identity and task lineage; preparation alone does not mark resumed. Refuse mutated/missing source, workspace mismatch, forbidden target and non-interactive absent consent. No automatic fallback to notes-only or terminal captures.
scope_out: Changing cdx or provider authentication internals.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Claude-to-Codex, Codex-to-Claude and same-provider fixtures recover the explicitly selected source with the intended cwd and target account.
AC2: Ambiguous/stale/deleted source, workspace mismatch and unsupported contract return a diagnostic and no launch; can-resume fallback-to-last cannot satisfy exact resume.
AC3: An ask-first target requires explicit consent for each transfer; blocked/never targets are refused and failed launch leaves the source interrupted.
AC4: Successful target launch records lineage while retaining separate native conversation ids and the original source evidence.

backlog_items.title: 2.7 Provider identity across watch CLI and desktop widgets
problem: Current views hide provider identity and can render absent metrics as ordinary values.
scope_in: Priority rationale: depends on 2.4 and 2.5; recovery action wiring follows 2.6.

Extend Go and QML payload consumers for additive provider fields, nullable metrics, quota provenance and schema compatibility; legacy missing provider defaults only when legacy payload provenance guarantees Claude.

Show provider/account on agents, usage and interrupted rows plus selection details; filter by provider without losing cross-provider global slot totals. Keep existing keyboard navigation, responsive layout and provider-neutral model display.
Wire relaunch selection to the shared guarded recovery command, showing native-resume versus cross-provider-transfer wording and exact target before confirmation.
Add mixed/legacy/unknown-data fixtures to existing Go render tests and widget fixture generators; use existing screenshot procedure instead of introducing another UI.
scope_out: Changing cdx or provider authentication internals.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Mixed snapshots display correct provider/account for agents, history, usage and interruptions in CLI, watch and both optional widgets.
AC2: Unknown context, price and quota render as unavailable with appropriate window/source labels; zero remains a distinguishable measured value.
AC3: Existing Claude-only fixtures and narrow-terminal navigation pass; mixed-provider renders are reviewable through existing screenshot commands.
AC4: Selecting recovery invokes the shared policy helper with exact source identity and receives the same denial/confirmation behavior as the CLI.

backlog_items.title: 2.8 Compatibility regression onboarding and delivery evidence
problem: A dual-provider fork needs a reproducible migration and proof that Claude-only users remain supported.
scope_in: Priority rationale: final integration after 2.1 through 2.7, with offline tests authored alongside each slice.

Update README installation and feature wording, account example and runbooks for dispatch, memory, interruptions, session retros and project work. Document Claude-only, Codex-only and mixed examples with invented profile names.

Publish the tested cdx version/capability matrix, guarded-operation limitations, supported provider flags, schema migration/rebuild behavior and rollback procedure. Preserve upstream history and MIT license attribution.
Run python3 -m pytest tests and go test ./... in tools/crow-watch; use fake cdx/native artifacts for success/error/race cases and generate mixed watch/widget renders.

Provide optional owner-run live smoke steps: one task per provider in separate worktrees, observe completion/usage, then an explicitly confirmed handoff. Record live validation as pending unless actually authorized and performed; no automated credentials or paid generation.
Record task-level AC evidence and refresh Logics indicators/index through the manager at delivery; settle linked product only after implementation acceptance.
scope_out: Changing cdx or provider authentication internals.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Offline Python and Go suites pass with no live account or provider executable required; assertions cover both providers and legacy behavior.
AC2: Documentation contains copyable launch/dispatch/handoff examples, exact capability checks and a safe rollback that retains private source transcripts.
AC3: Acceptance evidence maps every request AC to a passing check or explicitly pending owner-run smoke; pending required proof prevents implementation closeout.
AC4: Public diff contains no local/ state, credentials, actual private profile inventory or unrelated upstream changes.

orchestration_task.title: Deliver joint Claude and Codex support through cdx
plan: Wave 1 (High, 2.1): capture sanitized cdx 0.21.4 contract fixtures, implement shared boundary and account/provider policy. Validate Claude-only migration and deny paths first.
Wave 2 (High, 2.2): implement shared context lifecycle and capability-based guard enforcement. Gate unsupported operations before enabling Codex launch.
Wave 3 (High, 2.3): enable interactive and tracked headless execution for each provider, helper jobs, atomic global slots and isolated workspaces; validate with fake cdx.
Wave 4 (High, 2.4): normalize activity/session identity and cached native adapters; verify simultaneous mixed sessions and report deduplication.
Wave 5 (Medium, 2.5 then 2.6): verify usage/token arithmetic and migrations; add exact native resume and confirmed cross-provider transfer over task_002 recovery helpers.
Wave 6 (Medium, 2.7): adapt CLI, Go TUI and both QML widgets, render mixed/legacy/unavailable cases using existing UI conventions.

Wave 7 (Medium, 2.8): run offline Python/Go suites, review onboarding and capability matrix, record acceptance evidence and optional live smoke separately. Use Logics lifecycle commands; do not mark implementation complete during corpus creation.
